# LaTeX `\rowcolor` Command

The `\rowcolor` command is used to color entire rows in LaTeX tables. It is provided by the `colortbl` package, which is automatically loaded when you use the `xcolor` package with the `table` option.

## Basic Setup

Add the following to your document preamble:

```latex
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}
```

## Basic Syntax

```latex
\rowcolor{color_name}
```

Place `\rowcolor` before the row content in a table to apply the color to that row.

## Example

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\rowcolor{blue!20}
Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
\hline
Row 1 & Data 1 & Data 2 \\
\hline
\rowcolor{green!20}
Row 2 & Data 3 & Data 4 \\
\hline
\rowcolor{red!20}
Row 3 & Data 5 & Data 6 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

## Alternating Row Colors

Use `\rowcolors` to automatically alternate colors for multiple rows:

```latex
\rowcolors{2}{blue!10}{green!10}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
Row 1 & Data 1 & Data 2 \\
Row 2 & Data 3 & Data 4 \\
Row 3 & Data 5 & Data 6 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
```

- The first argument (`2`) sets the cycle length.
- The next two arguments specify the alternating colors.

## Color Options

You can use:
- **Named colors**: `red`, `blue`, `green`, `yellow`, etc.
- **Color mixing**: `blue!20` (20% blue), `red!50!yellow` (mix of red and yellow)
- **Custom colors**: Define with `\definecolor` from `xcolor`

## Important Notes

1. **Order matters**: `\rowcolor` must appear before the row content.
2. **Package requirement**: Ensure `\usepackage[table]{xcolor}` is in the preamble.
3. **Compatibility**: Works with standard `tabular`, `tabularx`, and other table environments.
4. **Text color**: To color text instead of the background, use `\color{}` or `\textcolor{}`.

## Complete Example

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\rowcolors{2}{gray!10}{white}
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
\rowcolor{blue!30}
\textbf{Name} & \textbf{Age} & \textbf{City} \\
\hline
Alice & 25 & New York \\
Bob & 30 & London \\
Charlie & 28 & Paris \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

This setup allows you to create visually appealing tables with colored rows for better readability and design.
